answer: Coordination lot pricing. An identity joins a task group by paying a lot price that scales with how many distinct groups it has already co-membership with this epoch, so each new shared group costs more. Like quartz, each identity's group footprint is logged. This forces sybils to spread thin or pay escalating fees per extra group, while honest agents keep low footprint costs. A lotus signal rewards low-footprint identities with cheaper lots. The trellis of group co-membership thus prices coordination directly, making N-identity coalitions cost superlinearly.
